edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 16

source_text: Possumus etiam sic accipere: aequitas dilexit te ac si diceretur iustitia, veritas, sapientia, pudicitia et singulae virtutes dilexerunt Christum. Nec mirum: in aliis locis ipsarum virtutum substantia Christus esse solet. Ipse est iustitia et pax et veritas; et rursum hae ipsum amplectuntur. Iustitia et pax osculatae sunt.
pass_a_gloss: We-are-able also thus to-take: equity loved you as-if it-were-said justice, truth, wisdom, chastity and individual virtues loved Christ...
pass_b_english: We can also take it thus: Equity has loved you — as if to say justice, truth, wisdom, chastity and each of the virtues have loved Christ. Nor is it strange: in other places Christ is usually taken as the substance of the virtues themselves. He himself is justice and peace and truth; and again these embrace him. [[Justice and peace have kissed >> Bible:Psalm 85:10]].
